items.title: Import AI 476: Creativity and RSI; Open Weight Models; AI in Space
items.summary: Clark's weekly read, including a benchmark claiming research taste has doubled every three months since December.

_homepage.note: The TasteVal result is the one to be sceptical about and read anyway: a claim that frontier models' experimental research taste has doubled every 3.0 months since December 2025. If anything like that holds it changes what delegating literature appraisal looks like, which matters more to a registrar than any model launch. Issue 475 came through here via the Substack mirror; this is Clark's own site.

items.title: Is the 200g UHQR of The Who's Who's Next the New Vinyl Benchmark?
items.summary: The Who is on his shelf, and this is the pressing that claims to replace every edition of it.

_homepage.note: Rated 11 for music and 10 for sound, which from Analog Planet is close to a coronation — but the useful detail is buried lower: Analogue Productions' own PR concedes this is not a fresh lacquer cut from the original tapes, it is built on the 2005 Classic Records edition. At $125 for one of 7,500 Clarity Vinyl copies, that caveat is the whole decision. The reviewer describes it as fatter, rounder and warmer than the 2023 Abbey Road half-speed it dethrones.

items.title: Introducing the Medical Guild of Australia
items.summary: Three doctors have started a new advocacy body for private practice, and it is currently a Facebook group.

_homepage.note: A GP, an ophthalmologist and an obstetrician have launched this under a name that deliberately echoes the Pharmacy Guild, which is a registered employers' organisation with real industrial weight. Whether this becomes anything is the open question, but the appetite behind it is the same frustration the AMA trainee survey picked up a fortnight ago. Worth knowing it exists before it starts appearing in the college-politics conversation.

items.title: IBCC: Intermediate and High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism
items.summary: Farkas folds STRATIFY, HI-PEITHO and PRAGUE-26 into one bleeding-risk number you can actually quote.

_homepage.note: The standalone hot takes on STRATIFY and PRAGUE-26 have both already been through this feed; this is the chapter where all three land together — roughly 622 patients given about 18mg tPA over six to nine hours, two intracranial haemorrhages, a 0.3 per cent ICH risk. That pooled figure is the one to carry, because every argument about catheter-directed lysis in submassive PE turns on bleeding risk rather than efficacy. This is the reference version, not the commentary.

items.title: EMCrit Wee: F/u With the 2026 ACEP Sedation Guidelines Authors
items.summary: The awkward questions about deep sedation, put directly to the people who wrote the new guideline.

_homepage.note: EMCrit 435 covered the new ACEP unscheduled procedural sedation guideline a week ago; this is the follow-up where author Mark Roback is asked about the artificial line between deep sedation and general anaesthesia, planned reversal, and planned intubation. Those are precisely the boundaries that get argued over at 3am when a shoulder needs reducing and anaesthetics is in theatre. Worth hearing the authors hedge their own document before someone quotes it at you.

items.title: Strike a Cord in Engineered Garments' Corduroy A-1
items.summary: The A-1 is the flight jacket nobody cites, and this is a cord version of it made in the US.

_homepage.note: The A-2 gets all the reference points; the A-1 is its 1927 ancestor, knit-collared and button-front, and much closer to the rustic end he actually wears than the leather bomber lineage. Engineered Garments cutting it in dark brown corduroy and sewing it in the States puts it next to the Woolrich and Pendleton shelf rather than the costume one. Good provenance writing on a pattern that rarely gets it.

items.title: Offworlding: Ambient House, 1992-1997 (A Mixtape)
items.summary: A guided way into the five years of ambient house that sit underneath the records he already owns.

_homepage.note: The shelf already holds the destinations — Moby's Reprise, M83, Tycho, Maribou State, Jungle — without much of the early-90s groundwork that produced them. This goes past the Orb and Future Sound of London into the rest of it, and as a mixtape it is a listening session rather than a reading list. Aquarium Drunkard's mixtapes keep well, which is the point of taking it now rather than when it is topical.

items.title: 5 Minute Sono: Pulmonary Contusions
items.summary: Five minutes on finding a lung contusion with whichever probe is already in your hand.

_homepage.note: Straight CCPU thoracic territory, and the short-video format means it is a genuine refresher rather than a lecture. The point it makes — that any probe will do, so there is no excuse to defer the look until the CT — is the bit that transfers to a trauma bay. Sits alongside the cardiac-output episode from the same series already in the collection.

items.title: RuneScape: Dragonwilds Summit
items.summary: First-party roadmap out of RuneFest: what December's Luminance update actually contains.

_homepage.note: This supersedes the Kuldra's Saga roadmap already in the feed. Luminance lands in December as a prelude to next year's Blood Crystal Saga — elves, Ceridwen and the bounty hunter Morwyn, elf cosmetics down to ears and facial features, and a Prifddinas-inspired building kit with arched roof pieces. Jagex also commits here to quarterly content updates plus monthly side quests, which is the detail that tells you whether to keep a save alive.

items.title: Hunter's Moon, a Historical Folk-Horror, Launches Oct 26 on PS5
items.summary: First-party dates and regions for a first-person folk-horror arriving a fortnight from now.

_homepage.note: October 26 in Australia and New Zealand, October 25 in North America — the sort of split that catches you out if you are pre-ordering. Worth flagging in the same fortnight as the Enshrouded 1.0 launch on the 15th, because it is the other PS5 release in the window that is built on atmosphere and place rather than a franchise. Straight from Sony's blog, so the date and platform detail are the authoritative ones.

items.title: Olympus Pen D: From Digital Street to Half-Frame
items.summary: Half-frame plus bulk-loaded cine stock, which is roughly the cheapest a roll of film can get.

_homepage.note: Rodrigo Aviles shoots the Pen D on bulk-loaded Kodak Vision2 250D, which stacks two economies on top of each other: half-frame roughly doubles the frame count, and bulk cine stock undercuts cassette prices before you start. For anyone whose shooting rate is limited by cost per frame rather than enthusiasm, that combination is the actual answer. It also puts the recently mapped Eastman Kodak range into practical use rather than price-list terms.

items.title: First Look: Gemini, Coburg's Wine Bar and Pantry
items.summary: One Coburg room doing wine bar, all-day eatery and bottle shop, which solves the walk home problem.

_homepage.note: 158 Sydney Road, run by Tresna Lee and Shane Farrell, split three ways so the pantry side sells wine, cheese, bread and craft beer to take away while the rest of it seats you. That makes it the useful kind of local — a place to sit, and the place you stop on the way back. The other Coburg item in this edition is five minutes further north on the same road, so the two make one evening.

items.title: First Look: Coburg's Italo-American Pizza Bar Hotel Lombardo
items.summary: A 100-seat Italo-American dive bar in a former Sydney Road bakery, and not a new-opening headline.

_homepage.note: 11 Sydney Road, up near the Moreland Road end, in a building that used to be a Lebanese bakery — a ten-minute ride from Brunswick and easy to have never walked past. Guinness, Americanos and Negronis, a beer garden, and pizza rather than a tasting menu. Filed here as a northside gem worth the trip rather than a this-week opening, since Broadsheet's October roundups have been worked dry.
